newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on USDA ending stocks data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on USDA ending stocks data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended weaker but well off the day's lows after USDA surprised the market by keeping its 1996-97 ending stocks projection unchanged in a report Tuesday, traders said.
USDA left ending stocks at 140 million bushels, above expectations for 125 to 130 million bushels.

USDA also raised its estimate for Brazilian soybean production to 27 million tonnes from 26.5 million estimated in last month's report. Brazil's exports were expected to total 5.2 million tonnes, well above last month's projection for 4.2 million tonnes.
Soybeans were further pressured by news a USDA analyst predicted U.S. exports could fall below 900 million bushels.
U.S. soybean exports are expected to drop by a record level in the last half of this marketing year due to plentiful South American supplies, a senior USDA analyst told Reuters.

Traders said they were impressed by the market's ability to digest the bearish news and still close only slightly below the 8-1/2 year highs set on Monday. The strong performance confirmed the bullish trend was still in place, they said.
Soybeans closed 9-1/4 to two cents per bushel lower with May off 4-1/2 at $8.55-1/2.

Soybeans closed limit up on Monday in anticipation of a cut in ending stocks and fell sharply when it did not materialize, but heavy fund buying boosted nearby contracts and the May and July traded higher in late dealings.
Traders said funds had invested heavily in the soybean market in recent weeks and were concerned it would turn against their long positions.
"Funds are going to buy until the trend turns down," a floor trader said. "Even with the bearish news we had we're only down four cents," he noted.

Commercials were mostly on the buy side. Cargill Inc bought one million bushels July and Term Commodities bought one million May, traders said and ADM, Continental Grain and Farmers Commodities Corp were small-lot buyers on the day.
Refco Inc reportedly bought five million bushels May and four million July but sold six million May. Cargill Investor Services bought six million July and one million May.
Rosenthal Collins bought 4.5 million May and Merrill Lynch bought two million each May and July.
In options, CIS sold 350 May $7.50 puts at 1-1/2 cents. CIS also bought 200 July $9.00 calls and sold 200 July $9.50 calls at 11 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 86,000 contracts, compared with Monday's volume of 94,782 contracts.
